external_merge_metadata_investigation.classification: external GitHub per-PR merge summary field disagrees with independent Git and its own timeline; internal GitHub cause unknown
external_merge_metadata_investigation.uniform_verification_rule: For every merged proposal require exactly one first-parent Git merge with frozen proposal as second parent, matching PR MergedEvent, successful native Actions at that exact SHA, scoped diffs and bytes. Retain REST/GraphQL summary comparisons as a separate check; do not drop any PR.

handoff_timing_observations.basis: Observer receipt file time to server retirement journal time; synchronized wall clocks; operational observations, not SLA/controlled benchmark

scope_limits: 60 synthetic clients with distinct mTLS identities, 20 concurrent client threads per host, tiny text proposals; not 60 LLM coding sessions or a controlled throughput benchmark.
Queued handoffs ran at the original one-build capacity; thirty builds were enabled only after all six retired. This does not guarantee cancellation of an already completing native merge candidate.
Registration still contends on the older writer lock; polling and handoff latency remain scaling work.
Trusted per-host accounts are shared among profiles; hostile same-account OS isolation is not qualified.
Existing sandbox Actions tested its Rust/workflow fixtures; broker Python suites ran natively on four platforms. No recovery-branch hosted-CI or full Rust/binary requalification is claimed.
100-identity and adverse provider/restart tests at this live scale remain open; native crash recovery regressions passed.
